source_text:
Fragmenta precationis et exorcismi
Ἐπικαλούμεθά σε, Θεὲ παντοκράτορ Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ οὐράνιε βασιλεῦ·
ἐπικαλούμεθά σε τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἐξορκίζω σε, πνεῦμα
ἀκάθαρτον, κατὰ τοῦ λόγου Θεοῦ τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν.
φοβήθητι τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον φῶς ὡς ἱμάτιον· τὸν μόνον ἔχοντα ἀθανασίαν καὶ
φῶς ἀπρόσιτον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Closing doxology after the exorcism command
orientation: The exorcist has just commanded the unclean spirit to fear God, and now closes the fragment with a doxology ascribing glory and dominion to God forever.
pass_a_gloss: We call upon you, God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king. We call upon you who made the heaven and the earth. I command you, unclean spirit, by the word of God who made the heaven and the earth. Fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment; the only one who has immortality and unapproachable light; to whom be the glory and the dominion forever. Amen.

choices.why: Glossary mandates 'we call upon' for this invocation formula.
Glossary mandates 'I command' for the exorcism formula.
Glossary mandates 'word of God' for λόγου Θεοῦ; κατά with genitive here expresses the authority by which the command is made.
rejected: according to the word of God

choices.english: who is clothed with light as with a garment
choices.why: Glossary mandates this exact rendering for the biblical image.
rejected: who puts on light as a cloak
who wraps himself in light as in a robe

choices.term: ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος
choices.english: to whom be the glory and the dominion
choices.why: Dative ᾧ with implied ἐστίν expresses ascription in a doxology; glossary mandates 'glory' and 'dominion'.
rejected: whose is the glory and the power

bible_refs.note: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν, φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον

pass_b_english: God Almighty, Lord Jesus Christ, heavenly king, we call upon you. We call upon you who made heaven and earth. Unclean spirit, I command you by the word of God who made heaven and earth: fear the one who is clothed with light as with a garment (Psalm 104:2), the only one who has immortality and unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). To him be glory and dominion forever. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: I command you by the word of God
last_rejected.why: The direct address 'unclean spirit' is omitted, losing the named addressee of the exorcism.
last_rejected.fix: Unclean spirit, I command you according to the word of God
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'Unclean spirit' as direct address before 'I command you,' so πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον is not omitted.

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered two ways; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use consistent wording across all sections.

variants.text: the only one who has immortality

problems.why: Same Greek phrase rendered two different ways across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one rendering across all sections.

variants.text: the only one who has immortality

edits.old: the only one who has immortality

fixed: The English already says 'the only one who has immortality' in the main text, but the literal gloss has 'the only one who has immortality' as well. The problem refers to the literal gloss rendering 'the one alone having immortality' which is not present in the current gloss. The gloss currently reads 'the only one who has immortality', which is consistent with the English. No change needed.
